statutorySection: Ind AS 109 (Financial Instruments: Recognition, Measurement, and Impairment) converged with IFRS 9 and aligned with US GAAP ASC 326
title: Financial Instruments: Classification, Measurement & Expected Credit Loss (ECL) Impairment

effectivePeriod.annualReset: Continuous credit loss matrix review, transition between Stage 1, 2, and 3, and forward-looking macroeconomic recalibration at quarterly and annual reporting dates
effectivePeriod.sunsetNotes: Mandatory standard notified via MCA G.S.R. 365(E) effective FY 2018-19 onwards.

plainTextSummary: Under Ind AS 109 (converged with IFRS 9 and conceptually aligned with US GAAP ASC 326 CECL), financial assets are classified based on the entity's business model for managing them and their contractual cash flow characteristics into three measurement categories: Amortised Cost, Fair Value through Other Comprehensive Income (FVTOCI), and Fair Value through Profit or Loss (FVTPL). The standard enforces a forward-looking Expected Credit Loss (ECL) impairment model that replaces the incurred loss model of legacy Ind AS 39. For general financial assets, a 3-stage model applies: Stage 1 (12-month ECL for assets with no Significant Increase in Credit Risk / SICR since origination), Stage 2 (Lifetime ECL for assets experiencing SICR), and Stage 3 (Lifetime ECL for credit-impaired assets). For trade receivables, contract assets, and lease receivables without a significant financing component, Ind AS 109 mandates or permits a Simplified Approach using a Provision Matrix, where lifetime expected credit losses are computed across aging brackets using historical default rates adjusted for current and forward-looking economic forecasts. Under Indian Income Tax law, an ECL provision recognized in books under Ind AS 109 is a non-deductible contingent provision disallowed under Section 36(1)(vii) read with Section 40A(9) until actual irrecoverable write-off, creating a mandatory deferred tax asset (DTA) under Ind AS 12.
